One who swears by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza must say none is worshipped but Allah, one proposing to gamble must give charity, and swearing by one's father is forbidden.
The Prophet showed anger at a pictured curtain, over-long prayers, a lost-camel question and insistence on night prayer, and disgust at spittle toward the Qibla; the strong control their anger.
Haya, pious shyness, brings only good and is part of faith; the Prophet was shyer than a veiled virgin, yet Allah is not shy of the truth.
The Prophet told those sent to Yemen to make things easy and not repel people, chose the easier way unless sinful, and said they were sent to make things easy.
The Prophet joked with young Abu Umair about his bird, called back Aisha's playmates at dolls, spoke gently to a man he called evil, and saved Makhrama a cloak.
The Prophet said a believer is not stung twice from the same hole.
Told not to pray all night and fast every day, since body, eyes, guest and wife have rights, Abdullah bin Amr pressed until allowed David's fast of alternate days.
A guest is owed a day and night's best food and three days' hospitality, without overburdening his host; Salman would not eat alone, nor Abu Bakr's guests without him.
When Abdullah bin Sahl was murdered at Khaibar, the Prophet let the elder speak first, offered fifty oaths, and paid the blood money himself when they refused the Jews' oaths.
Asked which tree is like a Muslim, Ibn Umar thought of the date palm but kept silent before Abu Bakr and Umar, and his father wished he had spoken.
Some poetry holds wisdom: the Prophet quoted verse when his toe bled, called Labid's line the truest, and prayed for mercy on Amir, who chanted verse marching to Khaibar.
The Prophet told Anjasha to drive slowly the camels of his wives and Um Sulaim, as they carried glass vessels, a phrase Abu Qalaba said others would be blamed for.
Hassan was allowed to lampoon the pagans in verse, with Gabriel's support; Ibn Rawaha's verse praised the Prophet; yet a belly full of pus beats one full of poetry.
Aisha was told to admit the brother of Abu Al-Qu'ais as her uncle, since Abu Al-Qu'ais's wife had nursed her, for foster relations forbid what blood relations forbid.
Leaving after Hajj, the Prophet found Safiya sad with her menses and exclaimed 'Aqra Halqa', but since she had done Tawaf al-Ifada she could leave with them.
In the Conquest year Um Hani found the Prophet bathing, screened by Fatima; he welcomed her, prayed eight rak'at, and honoured her shelter of a man her brother would kill.
Seeing a man driving a sacrificial camel, the Prophet told him to ride it, and when he protested it was a Badana, said 'Ride it, woe to you'.
On a journey the Prophet told his black slave Anjasha, driving fast the camels women rode, to drive slowly with the glass vessels.
When a man praised another, the Prophet said thrice that he had cut his brother's neck; one who must praise should say 'I think', for none sanctifies anyone before Allah.
Told by Dhul Khawaisira to act justly, the Prophet foretold seemingly devout men who would leave Islam like an arrow, marked by a deformed-handed man found among those Ali fought.
A man who had intercourse while fasting in Ramadan could not free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, so the smiling Prophet gave him dates to keep.
A bedouin asking about emigration was told it is hard, but since he paid Zakat on his camels, he could carry on from beyond the seas, losing no deed.
The Prophet, saying 'woe to you' or 'may Allah be merciful to you', told them not to become disbelievers after him by cutting one another's necks.
Asked when the Hour will come, the Prophet asked what was prepared, and hearing only love of Allah and His Apostle, said everyone will be with those he loves.
The Prophet tested the boy Ibn Saiyad, who answered 'Ad-Dukh', refused Umar leave to kill him, tried to overhear him, and warned that the Dajjal is one-eyed, unlike Allah.
Welcoming the Abdul Qais delegation, the Prophet ordered them to pray, pay Zakat, fast Ramadan and give a fifth of booty, and forbade four kinds of drinking vessels.
On the Day of Resurrection a flag will be raised for every betrayer, and it will be announced that this is the betrayal of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.
Say 'Laqisat Nafsi' rather than 'Khabuthat Nafsi'; do not abuse Time, for Allah is Time, nor call grapes Al-Karm, since Al-Karm is a believer's heart.
Ali never heard the Prophet say 'Let my father and mother be sacrificed for you' to anyone but Sa'd, as he shot arrows, perhaps at Uhud.
When the she-camel slipped and the Prophet and Safiya fell, Abu Talha covered her, and nearing Medina the Prophet kept saying they return repentant, worshipping and praising their Lord.
People may take the Prophet's name but not his kunya Abu-l-Qasim; a father was told to name his son Abdur-Rahman; the Prophet renamed Al-Mundhir and Zainab, but Hazn refused Sahl.
Ibn Abi Aufa said the Prophet's son Ibrahim died young, as there is no prophet after Muhammad, and the Prophet said Ibrahim has a wet nurse in Paradise.
Take the Prophet's name but not his kunya, for he is Al-Qasim who distributes Allah's blessings; Satan cannot take his form in dreams, and he named Abu Musa's son Ibrahim.
The sun eclipsed on the day the Prophet's son Ibrahim died, Al-Mughira said.
Rising from bowing, the Prophet asked Allah to save Al-Walid bin Al-Walid, Salama bin Hisham, Aiyyash and the weak believers of Mecca, and to send Mudar years like Joseph's.
The Prophet told Aisha that Gabriel was sending her greetings, and she returned them, adding that he saw things they did not see.
With Um Sulaim among the women in charge of the luggage, the Prophet told Anjash, his slave driving their camels fast, to drive slowly with the glass vessels.
The Prophet, best in character, would ask Anas's little brother about his pet bird, and at prayer time in their house led them in prayer on a swept, sprinkled carpet.
Ali loved the name Abu Turab, first given by the Prophet when he found him, angry with Fatima, sleeping by the mosque wall, and wiped dust from his back.
The most awful name in Allah's sight on the Day of Resurrection is that of a man calling himself King of Kings, which some said means Shahan Shah.
